terms.fr: Ordre des compléments et des adverbes
terms.pt: Ordem dos complementos e dos advérbios

en.title: Order of objects and adverbs
en.summary: With several objects or adverbs, English follows a usual order.

paragraphs: When a sentence has more than one object or adverbial, English tends to follow an order that is usual, and breaking it sounds strange. The direct object stays close to the verb, and adverbials of manner, place and time follow.

items: He went **to the shop by bus yesterday**. (place, manner, time)
I gave **him a book**. / I gave **a book to him**.

blocks.html:
PatternExample
verb + indirect object + direct objectShe sent me a letter.
verb + direct object + to / for + personShe sent a letter to me.
both pronounsShe sent it to me. (not: She sent me it, in standard usage)

paragraphs: With give, send, show, tell and buy, the person usually comes first without a preposition. If the direct object is a pronoun, the preposition pattern is preferred.

The usual order at the end of a clause is manner, then place, then time (MPT): He worked hard in the garden all day. Adverbs of frequency stand in the middle: before the main verb, after be and after the first auxiliary.

blocks.html:
PositionExample
beginningYesterday, I called him.
middle (frequency)I always get up early. She is often late.
end: manner, place, timeShe sang beautifully at the party last night.

paragraphs: Do not put an adverb between the verb and its object: I like music very much (not: I like very much music). This is one of the most frequent errors for learners.

items: Wrong: **I eat usually breakfast at eight.** Right: **I usually eat breakfast at eight.**
Wrong: **She plays very well the piano.** Right: **She plays the piano very well.**
Wrong: **He gave to me a book.** Right: **He gave me a book.**

ro.title: Ordinea complementelor și a adverbelor
ro.summary: În limba română, complementele și adverbele au o ordine obișnuită: mod, loc și apoi timp.

paragraphs: O propoziție poate avea mai multe părți secundare. Aceste părți arată obiectul, modul, locul sau timpul acțiunii. Ordinea lor obișnuită ajută la o comunicare clară și firească.
Obiectul direct sau indirect stă de obicei aproape de verb. Adverbele urmează adesea ordinea firească: mod, apoi loc, apoi timp. Adverbul de timp poate sta și la începutul propoziției.

blocks.html:
Tip de informațieÎntrebareExemplu
Obiect directPe cine? / Ce?Văd **un film**.
ModCum?Ea cântă **frumos**.
LocUnde?Locuim **în oraș**.
TimpCând?Venim **diseară**.
Mod + Loc + TimpCum? + Unde? + Când?Merg **repede la magazin acum**.
